item.title: Air Niugini to resume Auckland flights after 26 years
item.description: Air Niugini will resume direct flights to Auckland, New Zealand, after a 26-year absence, with three weekly services between Port Moresby and Auckland starting on November 17, 2026. Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer Alan Milne announced the return of the route in Port Moresby today after receiving International Airline Licence No. 29 from Department of Transport Secretary Matthew Wowoni.
item.content:encoded:
Air Niugini will resume direct flights to Auckland, New Zealand, after a 26-year absence, with three weekly services between Port Moresby and Auckland starting on November 17, 2026.

Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer Alan Milne announced the return of the route in Port Moresby today after receiving International Airline Licence No. 29 from Department of Transport Secretary Matthew Wowoni.

Mr Milne said the licence would allow the national airline to operate direct flights every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

The flights will take approximately five hours and 40 minutes and will initially use Boeing 737-800 aircraft before transitioning to the airline's new Airbus A220-300 fleet.

Under the new schedule, flights will depart Port Moresby at 9.30am on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, arriving in Auckland at 6.30pm local time.

Return flights will leave Auckland at 9am on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, arriving in Port Moresby at midday.

Mr Wowoni said adding New Zealand to Air Niugini's existing Australian and Pacific networks would strengthen trade, tourism and regional connectivity.

"The presentation of this licence represents a significant milestone for Air Niugini and Papua New Guinea as the national airline prepares to recommence services to New Zealand after 26 years. It is an important step in strengthening air connectivity, trade, tourism and people-to-people links between the two countries," Wowoni said.

item.title: Bougainville business partners warned to follow registration rules
item.description: The Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority is warning local and foreign business partners in Bougainville to comply with government requirements before starting business operations. Bougainville Immigration Manager Sylvester Vakore says some business partnerships involving locals and foreign investors have used the names of political leaders, including the President of the Autonomous Bouga
item.content:encoded:
The Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority is warning local and foreign business partners in Bougainville to comply with government requirements before starting business operations.

Bougainville Immigration Manager Sylvester Vakore says some business partnerships involving locals and foreign investors have used the names of political leaders, including the President of the Autonomous Bougainville Government, in attempts to advance their business ventures without following proper procedures.

Mr Vakore identified business registration as a key area of concern, saying local business partners must ensure their businesses are properly registered before commencing operations.

He said the registration process includes obtaining the necessary approvals from the Investment Promotion Authority, Internal Revenue Commission, Bougainville Investment Bureau and, for businesses operating in Buka, the Buka Urban Council.

Mr Vakore said the use of names of political leaders and other prominent individuals did not exempt business operators from complying with the required registration processes.

item.title: West New Britain schools end 2026 academic year early due to drought
item.description: All schools in West New Britain Province have formally ended the 2026 academic year, with classes suspended last Friday, November 6, due to prolonged drought conditions affecting the province. The decision was communicated to school administrations through a circular issued by the Provincial Education Board [PEB], advising schools to suspend classes and send student's home.
item.content:encoded:
All schools in West New Britain Province have formally ended the 2026 academic year, with classes suspended last Friday, November 6, due to prolonged drought conditions affecting the province.

The decision was communicated to school administrations through a circular issued by the Provincial Education Board [PEB], advising schools to suspend classes and send student's home.

Executive Manager for the Provincial Division of Education, Vincent Kalatia, confirmed that the PEB made the decision after schools had been affected by El Niño weather conditions since June this year.

Mr Kalatia said the severity of the drought had made it necessary to bring the academic year to an early close.

However, he clarified that schools wishing to hold their annual speech days or end-of-year class parties would still be allowed to do so after classes had been suspended.

He said school administrations could make their own arrangements for these events.

All teachers in the province have also been advised to begin their holidays early because of the ongoing drought conditions.

item.title: Six contestants vie for Oro’s Miss Bird of Paradise title
item.description: Six young women will compete for the Miss Bird of Paradise Northern [Oro] title when the 2026 pageant is held in Popondetta from November 9 to 14. The pageant will be staged under the theme, “Celebrating Oro’s Culture, Heritage, Leadership and Extraordinary Women.”
item.content:encoded:
Six young women will compete for the Miss Bird of Paradise Northern [Oro] title when the 2026 pageant is held in Popondetta from November 9 to 14.

The pageant will be staged under the theme, “Celebrating Oro’s Culture, Heritage, Leadership and Extraordinary Women.”

The six contestants will represent selected local-level governments [LLGs] across the province.

They are Evangelin Kania and Samantha Setiro from Tufi LLG, Theresha Diannah Orere from Oro Bay LLG, Jacobeth Bainda from Tamata LLG, Marie Louise Joekari from Higaturu LLG, and Patricia Abaija Tagete from Kokoda LLG.

Deputy Chairlady of the 2026 pageant, Kewana Irurapa, said the official program would begin on Monday, November 9, with a launch and float parade through Popondetta town.

The contestants will then take part in various activities throughout the week, leading up to the crowning of Miss Bird of Paradise Northern on Saturday, November 14.

Following the crowning, the winner will travel to Port Moresby with the provincial committee to prepare for the National Miss Bird of Paradise Pageant.

Ms Irurapa thanked the Oro Provincial Government and its administration for funding the event and called on the people of the province to support the pageant and its activities.

item.title: MoA to be signed between Moveave and Kamea tribes
item.description: Moveave and Kamea tribes in Gulf Province will sign a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on the 14th of this month, November, to end their long-running tribal conflict at Upper Taure, Hinenga, Fish Creek in the Taure Lakekamu Local Level Government. item.content:encoded:
Moveave and Kamea tribes in Gulf Province will sign a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on the 14th of this month, November, to end their long-running tribal conflict at Upper Taure, Hinenga, Fish Creek in the Taure Lakekamu Local Level Government.

The date has been set by the Provincial Executive Council, while the venue has been selected to be at Urban Malalaua Local Level Government, Kerema District.

The tribes met for the fourth time on the 31st of October to negotiate the venue and date for the MOA to be signed between the two ethnic groups.

It was revealed that a ceasefire agreement already exists, however it will be amended to capture the current concerns and grievances of both parties before the signing.

President for Taure-Lakekamu LLG, Herbert Pokana, and relatives of those who lost lives during the conflict, asked both parties if they wanted genuine peace and if they were serious about putting the issue to rest once and for all.

Both parties, after sharing their grievances on how the conflict has affected their livelihoods, agreed that they wanted peace.

The conflict reportedly started in September 2024 and has since resulted in loss of lives and several people injured. The ongoing conflict has limited access to basic government services for both communities and disturbed peace within Kerema district.

For the peace process, K300,000 will go to the affected families — K100,000 for each of the three families affected, and K200,000 will be shared between the two tribal groups — K100,000 each to make peace the Melanesian way with food and pigs.

Attending the meeting were community leaders, peace committee members and ward councillors from both parties, the Acting Police Station Commander – Inspector Pius Koma, and the President for Taure-Lakekamu LLG, President Herbert Pokana.

item.title: El Nino take toll on communities in Northern
item.description: El Niño has taken a toll on many communities and villages throughout the country, and Northern Province is no exception. The prolonged drought has left people without water, food and severe health issues.
item.content:encoded:
El Niño has taken a toll on many communities and villages throughout the country, and Northern Province is no exception.

The prolonged drought has left people without water, food and severe health issues.

With the National Government's initiative to address the El Niño issue in the country, a funding of 300 million Kina has been sourced from the World Bank to assist the people of PNG in these trying times.

The National Government made a decision on the borrowed funds where each provincial governor will receive K10 million while the districts will receive K5 million.

However, K2.5 million each has been released to the districts and provincial governments to conduct the first phase of the El Niño relief program.

While in Northern province, the three districts have received K2.5 million each together with the Oro Provincial Government (OPG).

The three districts of Northern province, namely Sohe, Ijivitari and Popondetta, have formulated their relief contingency plans to facilitate relief assistance to their respective districts.

Meanwhile, the OPG's K2.5 million has been strictly put aside for water supply projects in severely affected communities.

item.title: Biru CS opens new staff house
item.description: The Biru Correctional Service (CS) Institute in Oro Province opened a new staff house recently, marking a milestone achievement for the institution. Outgoing Commanding Officer, Chief Inspector Samuel Kiap, said funds for the staff house opening came from the institution's own internal projects such as poultry, cocoa and oil palm.
item.content:encoded:
The Biru Correctional Service (CS) Institute in Oro Province opened a new staff house recently, marking a milestone achievement for the institution.

Outgoing Commanding Officer, Chief Inspector Samuel Kiap, said funds for the staff house opening came from the institution's own internal projects such as poultry, cocoa and oil palm.

Mr Kiap said this achievement has come a long way with dedicated officers who worked closely under the management to achieve such a project in the institution.

He highlighted the importance of self-reliance, saying Biru is one institution that has succeeded from its own projects and has brought changes to the institution going forward.

Kiap said under his leadership, the staff house project cost the institution K60,000.

He said such good infrastructures are in place to boost the existing facility at the institution, and the asset must be kept in a good condition.

On this note, Kiap urged the Biru CS officials to work in unity and see progress at the Biru CS institution.

"We are out of support from the authorities, we at Biru can make a difference with the little we have," he said.

Mr Kiap has been in the position of Jail Commander for two and a half years and he will be leaving the institution to Acting Caretaker Commander, Senior Inspector Ludwick Monduk, while he travels for further studies overseas.

Kiap, under his leadership, also initiated and delivered single men's barracks housing 10 officials, built an institutional clinic, a staff house, cocoa fermenter and increased the poultry project.

item.content:encoded:
​For years, the sound of gunfire across Hela Province carried a single message: destruction. But on Saturday, November 7, a silent quiet fell over Komo Station—punctuated not by bullets, but by the thud of 120 factory-made rifles and more than 1,000 homemade firearms hitting the ground.

​In a province where tribal conflict has long cast a shadow over future generations, the mass surrender marks one of the most significant breakthroughs yet for Hela’s ongoing Gun Surrender and Amnesty Programme.

​Behind the staggering pile of surrendered iron lay months of exhausting, behind-the-scenes diplomacy. Community elders, traditional authorities, and provincial leaders spent sleepless nights negotiating with warring tribes, appealing to a shared desire to break the cycle of violence.

The programme was led by the Governor of Hela Province, Philip Undialu, alongside Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu, Komo Hulia MP Daniel Tindipu, Provincial Election Manager John Tipa and other prominent provincial leaders.

Mr Angu says the people of Komo have sent a powerful message to the rest of Hela Province: the time has come to put down the guns, embrace peace and build a better future for the next generation.

"Our children did not create these conflicts, nor did they create the gun culture that has caused so much suffering in our communities. Yet they are the ones growing up with the consequences of our decisions.

"It is our responsibility as parents, leaders and communities to change that story.

"We must ask ourselves one important question: What kind of future do we want our children to inherit? Do we want them to inherit guns, tribal conflicts, fear and destruction, or do we want them to inherit peace, education, opportunities and a prosperous society?

"Today, we must make a choice. We either continue investing in destruction, or we begin investing in peace, security and development. Hela cannot afford to sacrifice another generation to tribal fighting," Angu said.

He said the continuous loss of young lives, destruction of properties and disruption of essential services must come to an end.

"We cannot continue burying our young men, destroying our properties and denying our children opportunities because of conflicts that can be resolved through dialogue, reconciliation and responsible traditional leadership.

"Every bullet surrendered is a life potentially saved. Every gun removed from our communities is another opportunity for a child to grow up without fear," he said.
